How I work with them

01

Drafting tools

I delegate a first version of a Python converter or parser, written from a plain description.

I check by running it on real files and comparing the output with the source before anyone relies on it.

02

Print forms & protocols

I delegate the first draft of an HTML print form or the structure of a JSON medical protocol.

I check by importing it into the system, confirming every field renders and the JSON is valid, then fixing edge cases by hand.

03

Understanding the unfamiliar

I delegate explaining an unfamiliar error, query or API response in plain words.

I check by reproducing the behaviour myself, with logs, a SQL query or a Postman call, before I act on the explanation.

Different models. One thoughtful workflow.

Selected work

Things I
automated.

01

Price list import

2 h → 10–15 min

PythonExcelAutomation

The problem
Importing a price list meant copying every category ID by hand and pasting it into each service, so the system knew where to load it. It took a very long time.
What I built
A tool that takes the user's Excel file and returns a ready structure: categories, the services inside each one, and their prices, with the IDs already matched.
The result
A price list that is ready to import, with no manual ID copying. A job that used to take about 2 hours now takes 10–15 minutes.
Open the demo on GitHub ↗

A clean rebuild with synthetic test files and a test report. The original tool is not public.

02

Document import

40–50 min → ~10 min

PythonWordJSON

The problem
Documents were assembled in a constructor every time, by hand, to match how the Word file looked.
What I built
A tool that takes a finished Word file and returns ready JSON that can be imported straight away.
The result
The complete document appears right after import, with no rebuilding in the constructor. Per document, about 40–50 minutes became about 10.

The engineering approach

Problem first.
Then technology.

01

Problem

Which action repeats? Who needs the outcome? What would make the task complete?

02

Context

Identify the sources, separate data from instructions, describe the expected output.

03

Workflow

Decide what the model does, what follows a rule, and where a person chooses.

04

Review

Try different examples, return to the source, look for errors, keep the ability to stop.
